**5. The transcription audit found one real error in 232 readings.** Every

**State plainly what this audit does not cover.** It detects numbers that are
absent from the source. It cannot detect the failure that prompted it — a real
number taken from the wrong row, or a ratio reported as an accuracy, which is
what the RCP reading did. Those values are present in the document and pass
every check here. Catching them needs adjacency between a method name and its
value, which was not built. So 0.7% bounds one failure mode and says nothing
about the other.

**Screening for that failure found two more, and they diagnose differently than
expected.** A check over every defined concept — does the definition name a
versioned model that appears nowhere in its own sources — returned two hits, both
citing a paper called TabRank with circumstantial detail (NQ-Tables training,

`a2daecfa archive: discard 90 readings that no overthinking claim rests on`.
So these are not fabrications but **definitions left describing evidence that
was deliberately removed months later**, and nothing said so.

That is a structural gap, not an accident. `stale_analysis` checks hand-written
prose in *both* directions precisely because "evidence really did leave... the
prose describes sources the archive no longer holds, which is worse than
describing too few: a reader cannot find what it is talking about."
**Definitions have no equivalent.** `report_staleness` counts a definition as
outgrown only when its evidence *grows*; a definition whose sources are deleted
keeps its confident text and its shrunken count, and looks healthy. Both
definitions were cleared by hand, which CLAUDE.md sanctions for a definition
that is wrong rather than merely behind, and they will be re-derived. The gap
itself is left for a person: the fix is small and symmetric with the analysis
check, but it is a code change and belongs in a note of its own.
